openings.name: Italian Game
openings.blurb: One of the oldest openings. The bishop on c4 eyes the weak f7 square while you develop fast and castle.
ideas: Aim the bishop at f7, the softest square in Black's camp
Castle early and follow up with c3 and d4
Develop knights before bishops when unsure

openings.name: Ruy López
openings.blurb: The "Spanish torture". The bishop pressures the knight that defends e5, building a long squeeze.
ideas: Pressure the defender of e5 with Bb5
Retreat the bishop to a4 and b3 rather than giving it up cheaply
Build the centre slowly with c3 and d4

openings.name: Scotch Game
openings.blurb: Blow the centre open on move three. Simple, direct and full of active piece play.
ideas: Recapture on d4 with the knight
Use the open lines for quick development

openings.name: Vienna Game
openings.blurb: A flexible knight move that keeps the f-pawn free for an early f4 break.
ideas: Keep the option of f4 open
Bc4 often joins the attack on f7

openings.name: King's Gambit
openings.blurb: Romantic and sharp: offer a pawn to rip open the f-file and seize the centre.
ideas: Trade the f-pawn for Black's e-pawn to own the centre
Get the f-file open for your rook
Develop quickly – time is worth more than the pawn

openings.name: Evans Gambit
openings.core: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4
openings.blurb: Give the b-pawn to gain time for c3 and d4, building a huge centre with attacking chances.
ideas: b4 deflects the bishop and gains tempo
Open lines toward the black king

openings.name: Two Knights: Knight Attack
openings.core: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5
openings.blurb: Knight and bishop gang up on f7 right away. Black must be precise or get blown away (the Fried Liver).
ideas: Ng5 doubles the attack on f7

openings.name: Danish Gambit
openings.blurb: Sacrifice pawns for two raking bishops and a lightning attack.
ideas: Offer c3 to speed up development
Bishops on c4 and b2 aim at the king

openings.name: Bishop's Opening
openings.blurb: Bishop out first, keeping the f-pawn and knight flexible. A quiet road to Italian-style play.
ideas: Choose between d3 setups and an f4 break

openings.name: Ponziani Opening
openings.blurb: Prepare d4 with c3 to build a full pawn centre. Off the beaten path and tricky.
ideas: Aim for a big e4–d4 centre

openings.name: Smith-Morra Gambit
openings.blurb: A pawn for rapid development and open files against the Sicilian.
ideas: Recapture with the knight on c3 if accepted
Put rooks on c1 and d1
Use the open c- and d-files

openings.name: Alapin Sicilian
openings.blurb: Prepare d4 so you can recapture with a pawn and keep a classical centre.
ideas: c3 then d4 for a full centre

openings.name: Queen's Gambit
openings.blurb: Offer the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre. A world-champion favourite.
ideas: If Black takes, win the pawn back with e3 and Bxc4

openings.name: London System
openings.blurb: A rock-solid set-up you can play against almost anything: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3.
ideas: Pawns on c3–d4–e3 form a sturdy triangle
Ne5 and an h-pawn push can start an attack

openings.name: Jobava London
openings.blurb: The aggressive cousin of the London: Nc3 and Bf4 aim for an early Nb5 jump.

openings.name: Colle System
openings.blurb: Quiet build-up, then a powerful e4 break with pieces aimed at the king.

openings.name: Trompowsky Attack
openings.blurb: Pin and harass the knight on move two and drag Black out of the books.
ideas: Bg5 threatens to double Black's pawns

openings.name: Catalan Opening
openings.blurb: Queen's Gambit meets fianchetto: the g2-bishop puts long-term pressure on the queenside.
ideas: Bishop to g2 aims down the long diagonal

openings.name: English Opening
openings.blurb: Control d5 from the side and keep every option open.

openings.name: Réti Opening
openings.blurb: Hypermodern: let Black take the centre, then attack it from the flanks.

openings.name: King's Indian Attack
openings.blurb: A universal set-up – Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, d3, e4 – followed by a kingside attack.
ideas: Prepare e4 with d3 and Nbd2
Attack with e5 and h4 later

openings.name: Bird's Opening
openings.blurb: Grab e5 with the f-pawn and aim for a kingside attack.
ideas: Watch out for the From Gambit (...e5)

openings.name: Sicilian Defence
openings.blurb: The fighting reply to 1.e4. Unbalance the game from move one and play for a win.
ideas: Trade the c-pawn for White's d-pawn

openings.name: Sicilian Najdorf
openings.core: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
openings.blurb: Fischer's and Kasparov's weapon. The little move ...a6 prepares ...e5 or ...b5.
ideas: ...a6 keeps knights and bishops off b5

openings.name: Sicilian Dragon
openings.core: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
openings.blurb: The g7-bishop breathes fire down the long diagonal. Sharp, double-edged chess.
ideas: Exchange sacrifices on c3 are common

openings.name: French Defence
openings.blurb: Solid and counter-punching: build a wall with ...e6 and ...d5, then hit the centre with ...c5.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defence
openings.blurb: Like the French, but the bishop gets out before ...e6. Very solid.
ideas: Develop the c8-bishop to f5 or g4

openings.name: Scandinavian Defence
openings.blurb: Hit e4 immediately and bring the queen out early. Easy to learn, hard to crack.
ideas: Recapture on d5 with the queen

openings.name: Pirc Defence
openings.blurb: Let White build a centre, then undermine it with a fianchettoed bishop.

openings.name: Modern Defence
openings.blurb: Fianchetto first and ask questions later.

openings.name: Alekhine's Defence
openings.blurb: Provoke White's pawns forward, then attack them as targets.

openings.name: Petrov Defence
openings.blurb: Counterattack e4 instead of defending e5. Super solid.

openings.name: Philidor Defence
openings.blurb: Defend e5 with a pawn and keep a compact position.

openings.name: Two Knights Defence
openings.core: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6
openings.blurb: Counterattack e4 against the Italian and invite sharp play.

openings.name: Stafford Gambit
openings.core: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6
openings.blurb: A trappy gambit: give the e-pawn and set traps around the white king. Objectively dubious - strong opponents (like the level 10 bot) know the refutation, so you must fight hard.
ideas: After Nxc6 play ...dxc6 for open lines
Bishops to c5 and the knight to g4

openings.name: King's Indian Defence
openings.blurb: Let White take space, then launch a kingside storm. A favourite of attacking players.

openings.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence
openings.core: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4
openings.blurb: Pin the knight to stop e4. Flexible and respected at every level.
ideas: Often trade bishop for knight to double White's pawns

openings.name: Queen's Indian Defence
openings.core: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6
openings.blurb: Fianchetto the queen's bishop to control e4 from a distance.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
openings.blurb: Hold d5 with ...e6. Classical and very solid.

openings.name: Slav Defence
openings.blurb: Support d5 with the c-pawn and keep the light-squared bishop free.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
openings.blurb: Take the pawn, then use the time to develop and strike back in the centre.
ideas: Don't cling to the extra pawn

openings.name: Grünfeld Defence
openings.core: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
openings.blurb: Let White build a big centre, then blast it with pieces and ...c5.

openings.name: Dutch Defence
openings.blurb: Grab e4 with the f-pawn and aim for a kingside attack.
ideas: Guard the weakened e8–h5 diagonal against an early Qh5+

openings.name: Modern Benoni
openings.core: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6
openings.blurb: Create an imbalance: a queenside majority and a dynamic g7-bishop.
ideas: Trade on d5 to open the e-file

openings.name: Benko Gambit
openings.core: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5
openings.blurb: Give a queenside pawn for long-lasting pressure on the a- and b-files.

openings.name: Budapest Gambit
openings.blurb: Hit the centre with a surprise pawn sacrifice and win it back with active pieces.
